To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the time lower bounds on the tasks of computing various geometric measures of a convex polygon and the time lower bound on detecting whether a convex polygon lies inside another are Ω(log n), and that the time upper bounds on these tasks are also Ω(log n).

the time lower bound Ω(log n) for these convexity problems is tight for the mesh with multiple broadcasts, that the CREW- PRAM and the mesh without multiple broadcasting require Ω(log n) steps to solve these convexity problems, and that the mesh with multiple broadcast can be used to solve convexity problems on convex n-gons in O(1)-time.

Ω(log n)-time algorithms for the tasks of interest are optimal on the mesh with multiple broadcasts of size n ×n and that O(log n)-time CREW-PRAMS algorithms are optimal for all the problems except for the minimum-distance problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the complexity of geometric problems on a parallel model of computation that has been proposed as a model of computation for VLSI.
the complexity of geometric problems on meshes with multiple broadcasting.
the computational complexity of a set of fundamental problems in convex geometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mesh with multiple broadcast is the optimal model for solving the convexity problems on convex polygons in the sense that it is both time-optimal and space-optimal.
the CREW- PRAM and the mesh are equally powerful for solving convexity problems on meshes with multiple broadcasting.
the mesh with multiple broadcasts is as powerful as the CREW- PRAM for the geometric problems we consider.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown a tight Ω(log n) lower bound on the time complexity of a large class of convexity problems on the mesh with multiple broadcastings.

the Ω(logn) time lower bound on a mesh with single broadcasting for computing the area, perimeter and diameter of a convex n-polygon is also a lower bound on a CREW-PRAMS and a mesh with multiple broadcastings for the same problems.
we provide the first time lower bounds for a variety of convexity problems on the mesh with multiple broadcast and we also provide the first time upper bounds for these problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for many geometric problems, the CREW- PRAM is no more powerful than the mesh with multiple broadcasts.
a mesh with multiple broadcast is more powerful than a mesh with only one broadcast.
the mesh with multiple broadcast is a powerful computational model for solving geometric problems.
